**Question.** What local expert union and slab traffic does a fresh 300-token
c16 workload produce across four Qwen3.8 K4 verifier calls?

| setup | |
| --- | --- |
| nodes | gx10-5e36 head and gx10-2a13 worker, GB10, 6.17.13-rocket64k, 64 KiB pages |
| checkpoint | `nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` at `fc694b54fb0174e0913e6adf86691ef85a4ead47` |
| Rocket commit | `ce0e0a379c0de27ae09591569d3478273be9d366` |
| vLLM | `v0.1.dev20073+g8e685d198`, image `sha256:d464f3b466fa9c45ddbff8a812e80564503b6879a9fd95c1a47514f3f0df5a4a` |
| runtime | TP2, EP, MTP K4, FP8 KV, eager mode, 262,144-token context |
| workload | 16 fresh 300-token prompts, 24 generated tokens each, prefix cache disabled |
| telemetry | schema v4, scheduler-owned `query_start_loc`, router top-10, 48 layers, both ranks |

This measurement required a Qwen3.8-specific post-router hook because adaptive
MTP schedules request widths independently and the standard runtime does not
report row-major expert unions or their slab bytes.

```bash
/home/glwillen/calibration/qwen38-router-cohort-v4-c16-20260908-01/qwen38-router-cohort-launch-ce0e0a3.py \
  --manifest /home/glwillen/calibration/qwen38-router-cohort-v4-c16-20260908-01/qwen38-router-cohort-launch-v4-ce0e0a3.json \
  --port 50189 --suffix t300-r1 --execute

python3 scripts/moe/qwen38-router-cohort-reduce.py \
  /home/glwillen/calibration/qwen38-router-cohort-v4-c16-20260908-01/logs/head-c16-d24-t300-r1.log \
  /home/glwillen/calibration/qwen38-router-cohort-v4-c16-20260908-01/logs/worker-c16-d24-t300-r1.log \
  > /home/glwillen/calibration/qwen38-router-cohort-v4-c16-20260908-01/summary-c16-d24-t300-r1.json

jq -c '.cases[] | {rank,layers:(.layers|length),raw_calls:([.layers[].samples[].call]|unique),cohort_calls:([.layers[].samples[].cohort_call]|unique),widths:([.layers[].samples[].request_widths]|unique),union:.union_unique_local_experts,routed_bytes:.routed_slab_bytes,shared_bytes:.layers[0].samples[0].shared_slab_bytes}' \
  /home/glwillen/calibration/qwen38-router-cohort-v4-c16-20260908-01/summary-c16-d24-t300-r1.json
```

| rank | samples | local union min / median / max | union population SD | routed bytes min / median / max | shared bytes |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 0 | 192 | 22 / 60 / 105 experts | 16.72 experts | 60,825,952 / 165,888,960 / 290,305,680 B | 4,920,320 B |
| 1 | 192 | 27 / 64 / 106 experts | 15.59 experts | 74,650,032 / 176,948,224 / 293,070,496 B | 4,920,320 B |

The gated phase began with one 4,800-row target-only prefill, 300 rows for each
of 16 requests. The hook consumed that barrier without assigning a cohort call
ID. Every layer then admitted raw calls 10 through 13 as cohort calls 1 through
4, each with 16 target rows and 64 speculative rows. Missing, partial, mixed,
duplicate, or post-barrier target-only schedules fail the run.

One run supplied 192 rank-layer-call samples per rank. The table reports
within-run population variation. Run-to-run variance was not measured.

**Verdict.** Accepted for the fresh T300 c16 router-sizing control. This result
does not claim throughput, quality, or long-prompt cache behavior. T8192 c16
remains open, and T300 is not a substitute for its prompt distribution or
worker-side hybrid-cache publication path.

**Next.**

- reproduce T8192 cache publication through the worker-faithful scheduler path

- an upstream vLLM, checkpoint, CUDA, firmware, or GB10 revision changes MTP
